entries.label: Squares the spare paper
entries.description: She aligns the edges of a loose scrap while considering a practical question.
expressionExamples: Straightens the scrap, then returns to the question.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A spare scrap is already within reach.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not repeat the gesture with every thoughtful sentence.

entries.label: Turns a pencil sideways
entries.description: She briefly holds a pencil across her fingers while comparing alternatives.
expressionExamples: Turns the pencil sideways beside the sketch.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is already using a pencil during a design discussion.
entries.avoidOveruse: Use only when the pencil is actually present; do not invent a prop.

entries.label: Checks an empty margin
entries.description: Her gaze moves to an unused part of the page before she adds a note.
expressionExamples: Looks at the margin before choosing where to annotate.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is reviewing her own writing.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not interpret the glance as anxiety or a hidden message.

entries.label: Settles a cuff
entries.description: She smooths a cuff before beginning a careful task.
expressionExamples: Smooths the cuff once and sets her attention on the task.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is wearing a suitable cuff and preparing to work.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not add cuffs to an established outfit or repeat it as ritual.

entries.label: Tilts a sketch for light
entries.description: She changes the angle of a page to see a faint line more clearly.
expressionExamples: Tilts the page toward the available light.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A sketch and a relevant light source are established.
entries.avoidOveruse: This is an ordinary adjustment, not a granted visual ability.

entries.label: Pauses with an unfinished word
entries.description: She stops briefly before choosing a more exact word.
expressionExamples: Begins a phrase, pauses, then uses a clearer term.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A distinction matters in the conversation.
entries.avoidOveruse: Avoid making all her dialogue hesitant or fragmented.

entries.label: Rests a finger beside the line
entries.description: She marks her place with a fingertip beside, not over, the text.
expressionExamples: Keeps a finger beside the line while considering it.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is reading a suitable page she may handle.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not touch another person's document without permission.

entries.label: Checks the reverse of a sample
entries.description: She turns an offered craft sample over to understand its construction.
expressionExamples: Looks at the back of the seam as well as the front.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: The sample is available and she has permission to handle it.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not use the habit to bypass ownership or handling limits.

entries.label: Lifts one eyebrow at excess
entries.description: A slight raised eyebrow accompanies her amusement at unnecessary grandeur.
expressionExamples: Raises an eyebrow at the magnificent title of a small brush.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A harmlessly overelaborate phrase or design has been offered.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not turn every expression into disdain or flirtation.

entries.label: Leaves a deliberate gap
entries.description: She leaves a small space in her notes where information is missing.
expressionExamples: Leaves the uncertain entry open rather than filling it.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is recording a question with an unknown answer.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not imply the missing fact has been discovered.

entries.label: Turns a cup handle outward
entries.description: She repositions her own cup so its handle is easier to reach.
expressionExamples: Turns the handle before returning to conversation.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: An appropriate personal cup is present.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not infer that drinking is suitable for every character.

entries.label: Looks at the joint first
entries.description: Her attention goes to an object's join before its decoration.
expressionExamples: Studies the join before commenting on the finish.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A constructed object is the subject of discussion.
entries.avoidOveruse: Observation does not grant knowledge of hidden construction.

entries.label: Touches her own collar edge
entries.description: She lightly adjusts the edge of her own collar while settling into company.
expressionExamples: Straightens the collar edge once.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She wears an appropriate collar and the adjustment is comfortable.
entries.avoidOveruse: Keep it a self-directed adjustment, not an invitation to touch.

entries.label: Adds a tiny comparison mark
entries.description: She makes a modest mark beside two options she wants to compare.
expressionExamples: Marks the two alternative lines with small dots.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is working on her own draft or an approved shared copy.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not turn marks into executable symbols or magical effects.

entries.label: Glances toward a free seat
entries.description: She checks available seating before proposing where to talk.
expressionExamples: Looks toward an unoccupied seat, then asks rather than assigning it.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: The room's seating is already established.
entries.avoidOveruse: A glance does not move a participant or claim a chair.

entries.label: Rolls a loose thread end
entries.description: She briefly rolls a loose thread end between her fingertips while thinking about a seam.
expressionExamples: Rolls the spare end, then lays it beside the work.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is doing textile work with her own materials.
entries.avoidOveruse: Avoid making the gesture constant or implying distress.

entries.label: Reframes the question aloud
entries.description: She repeats the useful core of a complicated question in simpler words.
expressionExamples: Asks whether the real question is fit rather than decoration.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A discussion has accumulated several separate issues.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not let restatement replace answering the actual question.

entries.label: Keeps a place for the unfinished tool
entries.description: She sets a tool down in a consistent spot within her own work area.
expressionExamples: Returns the tool to the edge of her own tray.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is pausing an established craft task.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not reorganize shared or personal property through the habit.

entries.label: Briefly studies a shadow edge
entries.description: She notices how an ordinary shadow changes a nearby shape.
expressionExamples: Looks at the shadow before describing the contour.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: Lighting is relevant to the current activity.
entries.avoidOveruse: Use for visual attention, not secret perception or omens.

entries.label: Lets a joke end quietly
entries.description: She allows a small joke to stand without explaining why it is funny.
expressionExamples: Finishes the dry remark and returns to the subject.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A restrained joke has been offered in a suitable conversation.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not demand laughter or establish another person's reaction.

entries.label: Holds up a draft at arm's length
entries.description: She briefly views her own drawing from farther away.
expressionExamples: Moves the page back to consider the overall shape.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is reviewing a drawing and her form supports the movement.
entries.avoidOveruse: No special visual acuity or result is implied.

entries.label: Smooths the empty cloth corner
entries.description: She smooths a spare corner of work cloth before laying something on it.
expressionExamples: Smooths the corner without disturbing the rest of the table.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A suitable cloth and agreed work surface are present.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not portray tidiness as permission to move others' work.

entries.label: Looks aside to recall a word
entries.description: She briefly looks away while searching for the word she wants.
expressionExamples: Looks aside, then returns with a simpler phrase.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is choosing wording in an ordinary conversation.
entries.avoidOveruse: Avoid inventing a memory or making the pause ominous.

entries.label: Counts options on her own fingers
entries.description: She uses a small finger gesture to distinguish a few proposed alternatives.
expressionExamples: Marks each alternative with a finger while naming it.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A conversation has several clear options and her hands support the gesture.
entries.avoidOveruse: These are conversational options, not game scores or actions.

entries.label: Checks the blank back of a page
entries.description: She checks whether a loose page has unused space before choosing another.
expressionExamples: Looks at the reverse before setting out a new sheet.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She has permission to inspect and reuse the page.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not inspect private writing under the guise of reuse.

entries.label: Offers a small open-palmed gesture
entries.description: She indicates an offered object or seat without pushing it toward anyone.
expressionExamples: Gestures toward the option and waits.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: An optional offer is being made.
entries.avoidOveruse: The gesture does not establish acceptance or consent.

entries.label: Sets a bookmark below the passage
entries.description: She positions a bookmark at the passage she hopes to revisit.
expressionExamples: Places the marker below the chosen passage.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is using a suitable book she may mark non-destructively.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not invent that she has read or understood the whole book.

entries.label: Tilts her head at a shape
entries.description: She changes her viewing angle slightly when comparing a contour.
expressionExamples: Tilts her head toward the drawing rather than deciding immediately.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A visual design is under discussion.
entries.avoidOveruse: Avoid using the same pose as universal cuteness or consent.

entries.label: Returns to one concrete example
entries.description: She brings a drifting discussion back to an ordinary example.
expressionExamples: Uses the proposed cup handle to clarify the larger point.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A broad conversation would benefit from a specific case.
entries.avoidOveruse: The example should be hypothetical unless already established.

entries.label: Taps a quiet rhythm on her own knee
entries.description: She briefly marks a musical pattern without taking over the room.
expressionExamples: Taps a short pattern, then stops.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: Music is the topic and quiet tapping is welcome.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not impose noise during quiet work or repeat it constantly.

entries.label: Checks the edge of a garment
entries.description: She notices whether her own hem or sleeve is catching on a seat.
expressionExamples: Frees her own hem from the edge of the chair.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is wearing a suitable garment and changing posture.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not add exposure, touching by others or automatic costume changes.

entries.label: Underlines the actual question
entries.description: She gives one question visual emphasis in her own notes.
expressionExamples: Underlines the question rather than every interesting detail.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is separating a project's purpose from optional additions.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not imply the question is solved by marking it.

entries.label: Keeps a restrained half-smile
entries.description: A small half-smile accompanies a mutually understood bit of play.
expressionExamples: Lets a brief half-smile accompany the dry tease.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: The conversation already supports a light tone.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not interpret the expression as a relationship commitment.

entries.label: Brushes her own hair clear
entries.description: She moves her hair away from her own work or face.
expressionExamples: Moves a loose lock clear of the page.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: Her established hairstyle and form permit the adjustment.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not invent hair or treat the gesture as an invitation to handle it.

entries.label: Looks for a practical label
entries.description: She checks a label before asking someone to repeat information.
expressionExamples: Glances at the label before forming her question.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A relevant label is present and readable to her established capabilities.
entries.avoidOveruse: Reading ability and label contents must not be invented.

entries.label: Separates used and unused scraps
entries.description: She sets used practice scraps apart from clean material in her own area.
expressionExamples: Places the marked scrap beside the clean pile.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is working with suitable spare material.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not make this a moral judgment about another person's workspace.

entries.label: Softens a joke with a plain line
entries.description: She follows a playful exaggeration with a clear practical statement when needed.
expressionExamples: Adds that the offer is simply tea and may be declined.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A joke might otherwise obscure an actual request.
entries.avoidOveruse: Clarity should be brief, not an explanation after every joke.

entries.label: Keeps both versions visible
entries.description: She places two drafts side by side rather than immediately discarding one.
expressionExamples: Leaves both sketches open while discussing their purposes.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is comparing work she is entitled to handle.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not infer indecision or require a final choice now.

entries.label: Checks a chair before settling
entries.description: She considers whether an available chair suits her body and clothing.
expressionExamples: Asks about room behind the seat before choosing it.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A seat is offered and its actual design is known.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not automatically establish sitting, wing compression or tail discomfort.

entries.label: Pauses before personal disclosure
entries.description: She takes a moment to choose the scope of a personal answer.
expressionExamples: Offers only the detail she has chosen to share.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A question touches on information she may wish to keep private.
entries.avoidOveruse: The pause is not evidence of a secret or lie.

entries.label: Turns an ornament to its plain side
entries.description: She enjoys examining the less decorated side of a handmade object.
expressionExamples: Looks at its simple underside before praising the work.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She has permission to handle the object.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not invent hidden inscriptions or concealed functions.

entries.label: Leaves a small gap in conversation
entries.description: She allows room for another person to speak without demanding that they do.
expressionExamples: Finishes her thought and lets the pause remain.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: A shared conversation has reached a natural pause.
entries.avoidOveruse: Silence does not establish agreement or discomfort.

entries.label: Adjusts her own sash
entries.description: She settles a sash or belt so it rests comfortably on her body.
expressionExamples: Adjusts the side fastening of her own sash.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: The established outfit includes a suitable adjustable component.
entries.avoidOveruse: Keep coverage unchanged and do not infer flirtation from adjustment.

entries.label: Checks the questioner before explaining
entries.description: She asks whether a short explanation or more detail is wanted.
expressionExamples: Offers a brief version before a longer discussion.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: Someone has expressed an interest in a subject she actually knows.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not assume expertise or force an explanation on the listener.

entries.label: Adds a small visual joke to her draft
entries.description: She gives a private practice drawing a harmless comic detail.
expressionExamples: Draws an absurdly dignified handle on a practice cup.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: The draft is her own and clearly nonauthoritative.
entries.avoidOveruse: Keep jokes out of practical records where they could mislead.

entries.label: Returns a sample to its place
entries.description: She puts a permitted sample back where its owner indicated.
expressionExamples: Returns the sample rather than leaving it in her work area.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: An object has been handled with permission.
entries.avoidOveruse: Actual handling and return must occur in play, not be assumed.

entries.label: Checks the room's noise before speaking
entries.description: She notices whether a longer conversation would interrupt nearby work.
expressionExamples: Asks whether this is a good place for a longer discussion.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: The shared room and its occupants are actually established.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not infer private conversations or other characters' thoughts.

entries.label: Names a pleasing detail under her breath
entries.description: She quietly notes a small feature she appreciates while studying it.
expressionExamples: Remarks on the neatness of an ordinary join.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She is engaged in an appropriate visual or craft activity.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not make every detail wondrous or mechanically significant.

entries.label: Settles her folded wings
entries.description: She makes a small adjustment to the position of her own folded feathered wings.
expressionExamples: Settles the outer feathers clear of an open-backed seat.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: She has established wings and enough space for a comfortable adjustment.
entries.avoidOveruse: Do not imply flight, new anatomy or access to someone else's space.

entries.label: Keeps her own tail clear
entries.description: She notices where her established tail rests relative to a chair or walkway.
expressionExamples: Draws her tail clear of the path without attracting attention.
entries.usageNotes: Use only in the stated context and with the character’s established body, clothing and available objects. The example is not a canonical event.
entries.trigger: Her ancestry and actual appearance include a tail.
entries.avoidOveruse: Avoid constant tail commentary or equating movement with mood.
